transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start: 14:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Erin Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM), Lydia Chen (TidalShift), Marcus Holt (TidalShift), Rita Gomez (TidalShift Sec), Noah Kim (TidalShift)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding scope for TidalShift's pilot: goals are to validate latency/cost at target QPS, confirm networking + security (VPC/on-prem options), and agree next steps for pilot timeline and success criteria. Focus on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, initial data residency, and benchmarking plan.

Topics:
- Intro & scope
- Current infra & constraints
- Security/compliance ask list
- Pilot benchmarking and metrics
- Rollout timeline and next steps

00:00 Erin: All right hello everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Erin from Redwood, i'm the AE on this engagement.. um Lemme quickly, uh quick round of intros?
00:18 Lydia: Lydia, head of ML at TidalShift. we're building real-time anomaly detection for maritime telemetry. excited to get this moving.
00:30 Marcus: Marcus, platform engineering. i'll own the network side and the staging infra, and run the load tests.
:42 Rita: Rita, security lead, i'll review SSO, encryption and compliance needs.
00:50 Erin: thanks all. Samir, you wanna give a quick tech overview of what we'll cover from Redwood side?
00:56 Samir: yeah hi all. quick overview — Redwood provides hosted api endpoints, also Dedicated pools for reserved capacity, and Private deployments if you need VPC/on-prem. important bits we'll look at: latency SLOs, batching behavior, kv cache effects on prefix-heavy workloads, and model variant fallbacks. apologies, sometimes transcripts pick up KV cache as "key value cash" in our notes — ignore that.
01:22 Lydia: quick question, we have a mix of short queries and longer context windows (200-800 tokens), what will affect latency the most?
01:34 Samir: good q. throughput and latency depend on sequence length distribution and batching. longer sequences can trigger different kernel paths. also quantized model builds can reduce memory but slightly vary perf; we'll capture this in the benchmark.
01:50 Marcus: are there hard limits if we go hosted vs dedicated? we care about 99th pct latency under 300ms for short calls at 200rps.
02:05 Samir: hosted higher variability at peak, you can use Dedicated to get predictable throughput and SLAs — Dedicated pools are the recommendation when you need tight 99th percentile guarantees. we can scope first with hosted to iterate quickly, then move to Dedicated for pilot if results look good.
02:28 Lydia: what's the deployment model for data residency? we have EU-only data for some customers.
02:36 Erin: we support regional hosts and Private with VPC for stricter residency. Private gives you control over egress and data paths. there is also an on-prem option if you need air-gap.
02:49 Rita: on encryption, do we integrate with our K M S or Redwood provides key management? we're required to use our HSM for certain keys.
03:00 Samir: we do both. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can also work with HSM-backed flows. sometimes the transcription muddles it as "K M S" or "KMS" but it's just the same. we'll include the exact supported providers in the security pack.
03:20 Noah: network wise we need to understand VPC peering windows and whether there are static IPs for egress.
03:28 Samir: Dedicated and Private modes expose options for VPC peering; hosted can use private endpoints or NAT egress. for static egress ips we can provide egress ranges for Dedicated — i'll capture the specifics in the doc.
03:45 Marcus: ok good. timeline — we want to pilot in staging within three weeks, then production in ~8 weeks if benchmarks look ok. realistic?
03:55 Jules: that timeline is tight but possible — we'll need a prioritized list of blockers. first two weeks we do bench + security review, week 3 pilot ingest.
04:10 Lydia: success criteria: 99th pct < 300ms on short queries, cost under $X per 1k tokens (we'll supply target), and no PII egress.
04:25 Erin: great — we'll codify that in the pilot doc.
04:32 Rita: can you provide SOC2 report and any penetration test summaries?
04:36 Erin: yes — i'll email SOC2 and our most recent pen test summary.
04:40 Rita: (mumbles) and audit logs retention? we need 12 months of audit logs in our environment.
04:47 Samir: we have per-request tracing and audit events; retention for Hosted is configurable with add-on, for Dedicated and Private we can align to your retention policies.
05:05 Marcus: on the bench, what does Redwood need from our side? sample payloads? request patterns?
05:13 Samir: ideal: 1 week of representative request logs (anonymized), target QPS, median and 95/99 token lengths, any batching windows, and a few representative prompt templates. we'll build a script to replay traffic.
05:31 Noah: we can pull a week's data, try to scrub PII, team will confirm.
05:36 Lydia: note, some of our prompts include proprietary schema fields, will that be an issue for benchmarking?
05:44 Samir: not at all, we can run with your prompts in a staging environment; if you prefer we can obfuscate schema fields.
05:52 Marcus: cost modelling — any quick heuristics for Dedicated vs Hosted?
05:57 Erin: quick note: Dedicated is more capex-like but gets you predictable per-token unit cost at scale; Hosted starts lower up-front but can be more variable. Redwood Optimize can give model quantization and batching suggestions to reduce unit costs — we'll include initial recommendations.
06:20 Lydia: great. security follow-ups — Rita?
06:22 Rita: yes a few specifics: SSO via SAML, RBAC mapping to our groups, encryption in transit and at rest, K M S integration, and data residency policies. also we need a contact for any infra incident.
06:36 Erin: contact list — i'll include an on-call rotation contact for the SE/ops team.
06:42 Rita: also need evidence of vulnerability management cadence and any third-party sub processors.
06:50 Samir: we'll include vendor list and vuln remediation cadence. sometimes the auto-transcription says "vuln man" weirdly — but we'll make sure it's clear.
07:08 Lydia: operational runbooks — we want failover behavior documented: if a model variant fallback happens, what is the observable behavior for our app?
07:19 Samir: rollouts and fallback policies are explicit — you can do canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model if capacity constrained. we'll show expected latencies for the fallback path as part of the benchmark.
07:38 Marcus: integrations — does Redwood's API support streaming for long-running responses? we want partial tokens for lower-latency UIs.
07:45 Samir: yes streaming responses supported with chunking and structured output. may be slightly different per SDK but fully supported.
07:55 Lydia: ok good. next steps recap?
08:00 Erin: quick recap — action items plus schedule. Samir will prepare benchmark plan; i'll send security pack; Marcus/Noah to share logs and CIDRs; Rita to send compliance Qs; Jules will schedule follow up for Aug 18th.
08:15 Jules: scheduling now — i'll send calendar invite for the follow-up and block 60 mins for bench review.
08:22 Marcus: question — can you run the bench in our timeframe evenings? we have limited staging windows 10pm-2am PST.
08:33 Samir: yes we can do a dedicated window, we'll need the staging creds and exact IPs; we'll coordinate.
08:40 Lydia: anything else on integration? we may want to test embeddings + rerank pipeline for a second phase.
08:48 Erin: noted — we'll capture as phase 2.
08:52 Rita: one small callout: do you store prompts for evals internally? we need to understand retention and opt-out.
08:59 Samir: by default we retain telemetry for monitoring; we can opt to not store prompts for pilot or set retention shorter. we'll document opt-out options.
09:10 Noah: on the VPC peering — do you support transitive routing if we peer multiple VPCs?
09:18 Samir: typical peering remains non-transitive; for multi-VPC setups we support Transit Gateway style arrangements in some clouds or direct peering per VPC. we'll list architecture patterns.
09:35 Marcus: are there client libraries for our stack? we use Go + python async microservices.
09:41 Erin: yes official SDKs for python and node, and a Go community SDK; Samir can share examples.
09:48 Samir: i'll drop a go example and a load script.
09:52 Lydia: ok — pilot success criteria again: perf, cost, and no PII leakage — all agreed?
09:58 All: yes / yes.
10:05 Erin: last quick Q — do you have internal procurement constraints?
10:09 Marcus: standard PO process, need commercial terms for trial — if we commit to Dedicated we'll need a contract review.
10:16 Erin: we'll include pilot commercial terms in the follow-up email.
10:22 Jules: i'll send the invite now for Aug 18th 10am PT to review bench results — expect a 60 minute session.
10:30 Erin: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and invite; meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K M S" transcribed spaced out, "KV cache" sometimes as "key value cash"). few overlaps and filler words removed for readability but left some artifacts to keep transcript authentic.
